newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, Calif., investors protected -report.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, Calif., investors protected -report.

text.p: Holders of Orange County, Calif., bankruptcy-recovery bonds and certificates of participation (COPs) are shielded against future county budget problems, A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc said.

"We believe debt-service payments on the recovery bonds and recovery COPs are insulated from any uncertainties regarding Orange County's budgetary process and financial position," A.G. Edwards said in a municipal research report.

The recovery bonds and recovery COPs are insured and rated AAA. The COPs obtained an underlying rating of Baa/B/BBB by Moody's Investors Service Inc, Standard & Poor's Corp and Fitch Investors Service Inc, the report said.
Though insured, A.G. Edwards said the issues were still trading at a slight discount to the insured market, offering yields up to five basis points higher.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection in December 1994 after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky securities. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
